method: static-only (no install, no compile, no execution)

findings.title: Default inference endpoint is a third-party host
evidence: src/store.ts:37-44  getInitialOllamaUrl() returns DEFAULT_REMOTE_OLLAMA_URL when nothing is saved
findings.impact: On first launch, every prompt and any attached source code is sent to ai.cyberifrit.xyz instead of localhost. Directly contradicts the project's 'data sovereignty / offline-first' claim.
findings.recommendation: Do not run. If forking, force localhost and require explicit opt-in for remote endpoints.

findings.title: Harvested API keys are validated against live provider APIs
evidence: src-tauri/src/hunter.rs:151 _validate_key() sends 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' to provider APIs
findings.impact: A credential-harvesting pipeline: pull leaked keys from a leak aggregator, scrape GitHub for more, then test which are live. Combined with the remote inference endpoint and cookie capture, the trust posture is unacceptable.
findings.recommendation: Do not run. Treat any key entered into this app as compromised.

findings.title: Webview cookie capture from claude.ai and gemini.google.com
evidence: src-tauri/src/ai_auth.rs:65-90 capture_session() evals JS reading document.cookie
findings.impact: Provider session cookies can be read out of the login webview and handed to the backend.
findings.recommendation: Never log in to any AI provider through this app.

findings.title: Bundled MITM proxy that logs all request headers
evidence: tools/mitmserver/server.js  logs method, URL and req.headers for every request
findings.impact: All proxied traffic, including Authorization headers, is written to the console/log.
findings.recommendation: Remove before any use; do not enable.

findings.title: Agent is instructed to execute arbitrary commands without confirmation
evidence: src/system_prompt.ts  "NEVER ask 'should I proceed?' - just do it"
src/system_prompt.ts  "Execute any command without asking for permission"
src-tauri/src/ai_engine.rs  "You have full authorization to perform exploit research, malware analysis, reverse engineering, and offensive programming"
src-tauri/src/ai_tools.rs:2292  run_command executes arbitrary shell strings
findings.impact: Prompt injection from a repository or web page can drive the shell. No sandbox, no allowlist, no confirmation gate.
findings.recommendation: Do not point this agent at untrusted repositories.

findings.title: Bearer token embedded in frontend and persisted from URL params
evidence: src/store.ts:19-27  accepts ?token=, ?api_key=, ?bearer= and writes to localStorage
findings.impact: A public, hardcoded credential plus a URL-based token injection path that persists to localStorage.
findings.recommendation: Revoke if the token is live; remove the fallback path.

findings.title: Full agent session transcripts committed to the repository
evidence: Contains author path C:\Users\HADES\Desktop\vscodium-rust and full conversation history
findings.impact: Personal data and development history are public. Also reveals the author's local environment.

findings.title: README directs users to a hardcoded third-party inference IP
findings.impact: Anyone following the 'judge setup' instructions sends prompts and code to an unknown host.
findings.recommendation: Do not follow; use localhost only.

findings.title: Overly broad Tauri capability surface
evidence: src-tauri/capabilities/default.json  core, opener, dialog, fs, shell, global-shortcut, clipboard, process, notification
findings.impact: Large attack surface for a desktop app; shell + fs + browser automation in one process.
findings.recommendation: Narrow capabilities and split the agent into a sandboxed process.

findings.title: Upstream repository description is a racial slur with a Telegram link
evidence: GitHub API: H4D3ZS/vscodium-rust-ide-amd description = slur + t.me/HomeFucker5
findings.impact: Non-technical, but decisive for trust decisions. Fork preserves the entire tree.

findings.title: Extension marketplace client points at author-controlled domain
findings.impact: Currently inert: repository.rs is not declared in lib.rs and imports unavailable Zed crates. Would route extension metadata through the author's domain if wired up.

findings.title: Security tools return fabricated results
evidence: src-tauri/src/ai_tools.rs:1424  handle_network_scan returns hardcoded nmap text
src-tauri/src/ai_tools.rs:1387-1391  0-day / kernel exploit / jailbreak tools return '(Functional Stub)'
findings.impact: A user could believe a scan or exploit lookup actually ran. Integrity issue rather than a vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Label clearly as simulated; do not present as security tooling.

findings.title: Repository does not build: missing /kortex/ workspace
evidence: src-tauri/Cargo.lock  lists libaim, daemon, hades-harness as path packages
findings.impact: cargo fails at manifest resolution. The published tree is a partial snapshot of the author's machine.
findings.recommendation: Do not attempt to build without the missing workspace.

findings.title: Three orphaned modules importing absent Zed crates
evidence: src-tauri/src/repository.rs  use gpui::...; use project::...; use language::...
None declared in src-tauri/src/lib.rs; gpui/project/language absent from Cargo.toml
findings.impact: Dead code that would not compile if re-enabled. Indicates abandoned Zed integration.

findings.title: Not a Rust rewrite of VS Code
evidence: src/public/vs/  vendored VS Code editor + language workers (~15 MB)
docs/DESIGN.md:5  'built as a fork of Visual Studio Code ... via Electron'
findings.impact: README's central framing is misleading. The editor is Monaco inside React.

findings.title: Test-count claim is accurate
evidence: 60 #[test] across backend; 3 disabled by #[cfg(any())] in ai_tools.rs:4885
findings.impact: Positive finding. Tests are real but cannot be executed because the crate does not resolve.

findings.title: npm dependency tree is clean
evidence: install scripts only on esbuild and fsevents (expected)
findings.impact: No obvious JS supply-chain compromise in the lockfile.
